title: Modularity
hook: When changing one thing breaks three others, your business is too tangled together.
statement: Systems work better when their parts can be separated.
explainer: If everything's fused, every fix is risky and nothing can be handed off. Separate pieces can be improved, swapped, or delegated without bringing down the rest.
sop: Map your system and mark where two functions depend on each other.
Score how tangled each dependency is 1 to 10.
Split the most tangled pair into two parts with a clear handoff.
Give each part its own owner, process, or tool.
Change one part and confirm the rest keeps running.
equation_example: You have 3 Independent Modules, parts you can change without breaking the others. So Flexibility = 3. Higher means more of your business can be improved or handed off on its own. At 1, everything's fused and one change risks it all.
question: Name one tangled part of your business you'd separate first.
closing_statement: Separate parts move faster than fused ones.
caption:
Principle Nº 127: Modularity

When changing one thing breaks three others, your business is too tangled together.

Systems work better when their parts can be separated.

Your turn: Name one tangled part of your business you'd separate first.
